learning: Hypotheses: (1) the iteration-0 failure was under-turning and drift, not oscillation, since steering_oscillation was low; (2) the wider span removes line loss; (3) if the robot still leaves the track with no line loss, the limit is turning authority, so a forward array or lower mass is next. Watch completion_time on any finished run to judge whether base_speed can rise.
notes: Adopts the Builder's 50 mm span and changes only the controller: base_speed 1.8 to 1.4, kp 3.0 to 4.0, kd 0.1 to 0.3. Iteration 0 showed low jitter and max_error at the off-track floor, so the aim is more turning response and earlier correction, not less gain.
rationale: Iteration 0 ran off track on all 60 trials with progress of only 0.04 to 0.115, max_error at the 0.06 m floor, one line-loss event per track, and low steering_oscillation (0.065 to 0.073). The low jitter means the baseline was not oscillating, so the failure is the robot drifting off the line early, not chattering around it. The Builder's 50 mm span (x = ±0.025 m) should cover the drift that caused the line loss. I keep that geometry unchanged so the controller is judged on the same hardware the Builder proposed. For the controller, I lower base_speed from 1.8 to 1.4. At the 0.04 m lookahead, 1.8 gives the robot less time to correct before it leaves the tape, and 1.4 (PWM base about 2870) still gives a usable speed, though finishing under 3 s will need about 1.5 m/s average. I raise kp from 3.0 to 4.0 so each unit of signal produces more wheel differential (about ±1400 PWM at the usual signal size), since the robot appears to be under-turning rather than oscillating. I raise kd from 0.1 to 0.3 to damp the faster steering response. ki stays at 0.1 for the fixed motor mismatch. line_loss stays 'last_direction'. Expected result: fewer off-track exits and higher progress, with line_loss_events at or near 0. If the run still leaves the track with no line loss, the limit is turning authority or the sensor position, and I will test a forward array or a lower mass next. This is a prediction, not a measured result.
